verdicts.quoted_span: General Laws c. 40P, § 2, "broadly prohibits any regulatory scheme based upon or implementing rent control."
verdicts.reason: The SJC opinion says Massachusetts has a statewide statutory ban on rent control. The petition to repeal it was barred from the 2026 ballot, so Cambridge cannot impose rent increase limits.

No Cambridge-specific document addresses security deposits. Retrieved passage D052 describes a security deposit statute (treble damages, 5% interest), which indicates a state rule exists rather than its absence, so a no_rule verdict is not supported.

DX13 says MGL Ch 186 §15B forbids Massachusetts landlords from charging application fees, although brokers may charge them. That is an existing restriction, not an absence of rule, so no_rule is not supported.

verdicts.quoted_span: The policy order directs the city manager work with relevant city departments to draft policy options or ordinance language that will be presented back to council later this term.
verdicts.reason: The council only passed a policy order initiating steps toward a ban, and state bills are still pending. This indicates no algorithmic rent-setting ban was in effect in Cambridge at the time of the article.
